feedback.problem:
The hyperbola ${y}^{2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{15}=1$ intersects the line $y=-1$ at

$($
{{field-1}}, 
{{field-2}} $).$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the points where the hyperbola intersects the line $y=-1,$ we substitute $y=-1$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{15} & =1 \\ (-1)^{2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{15} & =1 \\ 1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{15} & =1 \\ -{x}^{2} & =0 \\ x & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the hyperbola intersects the vertical line $y=-1$  at $(0,-1).$
